avis.titre: The Only Sunscreen My Skin Actually Loves
avis.texte: I love this sunscreen so much, which is something I never thought I would say about an SPF. It feels more like skincare than sunscreen. It is lightweight, hydrating, and actually comfortable to wear all day. My skin stays calm and moisturized instead of tight, greasy, or irritated. What really sold me is that it works beautifully on sensitive skin. It layers well under makeup, does not pill, and does not leave my face feeling heavy. I actually want to use this every morning, which means I finally use sunscreen consistently. For anyone who struggles to find an SPF that feels good on the skin, this one is a win.

I have a really hard time finding sunscreens that work for me. I have pretty sensitive skin/eyes, and I am rather pale. Both of these facts make it difficult for me to find something that works hard enough but also doesn't bother my skin. This one strikes the balance. I love that the texture isn't too thick, but more of a milky consistency. It feels a little oily immediately after applying but dries down very quickly. I have had no issues with breakouts or irritation at all, which was deeply impressive to me as I often have at least one breakout when starting a new sunscreen. The only drawback is the price. For the amount it costs, it is really not enough product in my opinion. Yes it's fantastic, but I don't think it needs to cost so much for so little. Because of the price I'm not sure I'll be repurchasing it, which is really disappointing because it's a great product.

avis.titre: Great for sensitive skin; bottle needs a redesign

No pilling when i applied Glossier Stretch Balm Concealer under my eyes and Merit Flush Balm to my cheeks. I have worn this outside and did not burn when I was outside for 3 hours. The bottle is in need of a redesign. Both ends of the bottle need a flat surface. Currently only the yellow cap has a flat surface. This makes for an awkward user experience when after squeezing product out of the blue bottle, it cannot stand up on it's own and must be set down on its side. I do like the squeeze tip - it's is small enough to allow good control of how much product you want to use.

I will be the first to admit I have never wanted to use a daily sunscreen because I was worried about how it would look and it's just one more step on busy mornings. FAB Sunscreen Milk pokes holes in my justifications for not protecting my skin. I'm making it a point now to use this at least each morning and to reapply if i know I'll be outside later in the day. Pros: This sunscreen is easy to apply over your entire skincare regimen with the right timing. It doesn't leave a weird texture IF you apply it right. It has a faint smell that doesn't linger. I feel good knowing I "did the right thing" each morning. Reapplication later in the day if needed is no-fuss. Cons: There's a learning curve to application, but it's not steep. The penalties for said learning curve lead to weird textures and/or pilling. Be careful around your eyes (should go without saying… but I still made this mistake of being too careless a time or two). Tips: Don't rub it in, pat or daub it in gently. This helps with texture and keeping it out of your eyes. Use a small amount at first and add more if your application fell short. If you're extra worried about texture, wait a few minutes before applying any sunscreen. Try not to touch your face until the sunscreen has also had a few minutes. For reference, I use several of The Ordinary products in my skincare routine. So texture was a huge problem at first. I had pilly skin and stinging eyes at least a few days. My issues were not waiting long enough between

avis.titre: Ditch the chemicals and the lies
avis.texte: Research these ingredients!!! Do not put this on your skin or use at the beach! This is full of ingredients which are harmful. Get informed about what is in your skincare products before you blindly follow the claims on products. It's pretty terrible to be marketing this as organic UV filters, completely taking advantage of the general populations understanding of the word organic when used in marketing especially in recent years. The chemicals are considered organic simply because they are carbon containing compounds - they are still synthetic chemicals and some have been shown now to become toxic when exposed to sunlight after just a short period and can be harmful to your skin and microbiome and could accumulate in your body causing more harm.

avis.titre: A Sunscreen That Hydrates Like Skincare
avis.texte: Finding a sunscreen that delivers strong protection without drying out my skin can be challenging, but First Aid Beauty's Hydrating Sunscreen Milk SPF 45 checks all the boxes! It's lightweight, moisturizing, and soothing—perfect for my combination skin that leans dry. This formula is more like a hydrating lotion than a typical sunscreen. It absorbs beautifully, leaving my skin soft, plump, and dewy without feeling greasy. Colloidal oatmeal is a standout ingredient—it calms and nourishes my skin while providing an extra boost of moisture. There is no chalky cast, no pilling, and it layers seamlessly under makeup. With broad-spectrum SPF 45, I feel well-protected from UVA/UVB rays throughout the day. I appreciate that it's fragrance-free and safe for sensitive skin, so I can use it even when my skin feels reactive. Unlike mineral sunscreens, this one doesn't make my skin feel tight or dry—it feels like skincare first, sunscreen second. This is a winner if you're looking for a hydrating, non-irritating sunscreen that works well with other products in your routine. It keeps my skin moisturized without clogging pores, and the smooth finish makes it ideal for everyday wear. First Aid Beauty nailed it with this one!

I am a sunscreen fanatic and am really one of those people who applies every 2 hours—even when it's not sunny or I am inside. I go through a lot of sunscreen and this one checks all the boxes for me! First, it feels like skincare when it goes on, which is a huge plus! I am very dry and found this to be hydrating. It absorbed really easily and did not leave behind any greasy or oily feeling. Another thing that's important to me is whether or not a sunscreen will irritate my eyes. I am a runner and can't stand feeling that sting halfway through my run! This sunscreen passed my sweating and running test—I found that it stayed put and did not drip down my face or into my eyes.
